prompt: Which of these is the correct definition of the complexity class NP?
choices: The set of decision problems solvable by some algorithm in polynomial time
The set of decision problems where, for every 'yes' instance, a certificate exists that can be checked in polynomial time
The set of decision problems that are provably impossible to solve in polynomial time
The set of optimization problems that have no known greedy solution

prompt: Why is every problem in P automatically also in NP?
choices: Because P and NP are defined to be the same set by convention
Because if you can solve a problem in polynomial time, you can verify any candidate answer in polynomial time simply by solving it yourself and comparing
Because NP only contains problems that are provably harder than anything in P
Because a polynomial-time algorithm always produces a certificate as a side effect
